set.typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. Projects creating seven or more for-sale units, residential parcels, mobile home parcels or converted condominiums must restrict 15% of units for sale to moderate, low or very low income households; rental projects are exempt from the inclusionary requirement but pay the Affordable Housing Impact Fee under Chapter 18.05 (record below). Alternatives (18.02.050): in-lieu fees at the rate in the Council fee schedule (the certified 2023-2031 Housing Element, Program 2.8, states the inclusionary in-lieu fee and the housing impact fee are both currently $25 per square foot following the 2021 feasibility study), payable at building permit with deferral to certificate of occupancy allowed if the Council finds it aids feasibility and security is provided; off-site units within one mile; land dedication yielding at least 10% more affordable units than otherwise required. In-lieu fees are deposited to the City's housing trust fund for construction of new low and very low income units. Adopted November 2004, amended 2013, 2021 and by Ordinance 1062 (introduced August 24, 2023, adopted September 14, 2023) to update definitions, mobile home sales procedures and eligibility. The City may require more than 15% only when it provides a grant, subsidy, loan, fee waiver or other fiscal benefit.

set.typical_award_size: Not a subsidy. On Housing Element opportunity sites (Table F-10 sites outside the Town Center Specific Plan), multifamily projects with 20% or more of units affordable to lower income households get by-right approval (objective standards only) with ministerial design review under 17.50.045; other projects follow normal zoning review. Rezone sites carry a 20 du/ac minimum and 40 du/ac maximum, 60% coverage, three stories and a 35-foot top plate (40 feet for vertical mixed use), and at least 16 units are allowed on every site. Any project may request a deviation from a standard that physically precludes its proposed density, limited to the minimum needed. Lot consolidation incentives (deviations from development and subdivision standards) are available only to projects that merge a parcel under one-half acre with an adjacent parcel and are 100% deed restricted for 55 years (rentals at or below 80% AMI, ownership at or below 120% AMI, residential at least 85% of mixed-use floor area). On Mixed-Use Rezone sites residential uses must occupy less than 70% of gross floor area; no affordable exception is stated. Chapter adopted December 4, 2024 (Ordinance 16.142) and rewritten June 18, 2025 (Ordinance 16.142.1) to carry out Housing Element Programs H-1.1 and H-1.2.
